title: Green GDP: Unraveling the Diverse Challenges and Opportunities for a Sustainable Future

limitations: Entropy-step OCR on page 11 fuses several formulas.
Figure 12 caption collides with body text.

tasks: Task 1: Choose a GGDP definition with a measurable climate effect
Task 2: Estimate the global climate-mitigation effect of the switch
Task 3: Judge whether the switch is worthwhile after resistance
Task 4: Apply the shift to China by sector and policy decade

contributions.summary: Chooses the subtraction form of GGDP over ecosystem-service addition because the latter is still conceptual.
Reports a 31.57 percent average slowdown in climate-index decline, and a 5.23 percent exception in crisis years.
Prices multilateral resistance by the vertical distance of red-cluster countries.
EPS monetizes avoided deaths at RMB 1.6 trillion and climate benefits at RMB 2.9 trillion by 2050.

dependency_graph.handoff: GGDP series is the regressor for the climate index
Delta-CI gap is monetized as potential upside
National GDP-GGDP gap is the denominator of sector cost shares

assumptions.summary: GDP and GGDP growth-rate targets are the same after the switch.
Natural climate forcing stays constant, so CI gaps are policy effects.
The switch is simultaneous and takes about one year.
Resistance does not become a general war.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: GDP from World Bank WDI; resource and damage costs from OECD and EPA; China sector output from the statistical yearbook.
Low-performance climate indicators are inverted before TOPSIS.

models.summary: IEW-TOPSIS climate index plus linear CI regression.

verification.summary: PU stays below PD in almost every year since 2000.
EPS baseline versus GGDP-adopted emissions path through 2050.

results_trace.summary: World GI rises from 2000 to 2021, with spikes in 2008 and 2020 that reverse afterward.
GGDP path cuts the average CI decline by 31.57 percent; crisis years only 5.23 percent.
The GGDP switch is judged worthwhile because potential downside exceeds potential upside.
Manufacturing, agriculture, transport, and residential hold 89.2 percent of China's environmental cost.
Avoided premature deaths RMB 1.6 trillion; climate benefits RMB 2.9 trillion at 2018 prices.

writing_logic.summary: Abstract moves First, Subsequently, In addition, Furthermore, In the end, one model block each.
Method survey first, then a reason to reject the less established definition, then the identity.
Figure, then the sentence 'three conclusions can be made', then numbered readings.
Each k-means color is given an attitude, not just a centroid.
Strengths and weaknesses use a short claim as a heading and a paragraph underneath.

language_observations.summary: Human ordinal is First / Subsequently / In addition / Furthermore / In the end, not a mechanical Firstly-Secondly list.
Each assumption is a short claim; the Explanation paragraph does the justifying. Assumption 4 inflates into Latinate prose and is a boundary, not a model.
Choice is argued by maturity: the subtraction definition is more established because ecosystem services are still being conceptualized.
Chart reading is numbered and historical: crisis years are narrated as a spike and a rebound, not only as a coefficient.
Cluster narrative names the color, the economic trait, and the political attitude in that order.
Short-claim heading plus evidence paragraph. The diction turns purple (facile, arduous) and should not be copied.
Memo keeps To and Subject lines, restates three numbers, and closes with a hearing-from-you sentence rather than a slogan.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Rejecting the fashionable ecosystem-service add-on for a workable subtraction is the kind of judgment a policy problem rewards.
A headline percent plus a crisis exception reads as a checked claim rather than a single optimistic number.
Pricing political resistance, even roughly, answers the problem's negotiation task instead of stopping at a climate benefit.

weaknesses.summary: One GGDP formula is forced onto countries with different data.
Multilateral-resistance costs are subjective; k and b are not identified.
EPS inputs come from studies that may not share assumptions.
The prose swaps the regression's dependent and independent variables.

independent_extensions.summary: Estimate the monetizing slope from an external social cost of carbon instead of a free k.
Refit CI on a scaled GGDP so the slope is interpretable.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Prefer a mature accounting identity over a conceptually unfinished one when the problem asks for a measurable effect.
A global policy model should price who resists, not only who benefits.

unresolved_questions.question: What data identify the monetizing constants k and b in the upside and resistance equations?
Why does the prose call CI the independent variable when equation 15 regresses CI on GGDP?
